terms.gloss: it irks, it vexes; one is loath to, one is sorry for
terms.grammar: impersonal verb: accusative of the person, with the genitive of the thing or an infinitive (mē piget)
evidence: Plaut. Ps. 281: Nimiō id quod pudet facilius fertur quam illud quod piget.
Ter. Ad. 3.3.37: frātris mē quidem piget pudetque (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Donatus on that line: pudet quod turpe est; piget quod dolet. Nisi piget, if you don’t mind.

phrases.latin: Nimiō id quod pudet facilius fertur quam illud quod piget. Nōn dedisse istunc pudet: mē quia nōn accēpī piget.
phrases.english: What shames a man is far easier to bear than what vexes him. He is ashamed of not having paid; I am vexed at not having been paid.

phrases.latin: Adulēscēns, quaesō hercle ēloquere tuom mihi nōmen, nisi piget.
phrases.english: Young man, do please tell me your name, if you don’t mind.

sources: Lewis & Short: pigeo
